description_medium: Flexible polymer foams yield when cell walls buckle and collapse, absorbing energy as they densify. The stress plateau around this value is prized for cushioning. Strain rate and temperature swing the response in real products. The number is for an open cell polyurethane foam in compression.
label: Foam
summary_short: Flexible polymer foams yield when cell walls buckle and collapse, absorbing energy as they densify.

description_medium: Articular cartilage yields at low stress in compression because it is mostly water constrained by a collagen network. Permeability and rate control the response, which is why joints feel different under fast and slow loading. Degeneration lowers this threshold further. The value is for healthy tissue under confined compression.
label: Cartilage
summary_short: Articular cartilage yields at low stress in compression because it is mostly water constrained by a collagen network.

description_medium: Soft elastomeric rubber shows a low apparent yield because long polymer chains uncoil and slide instead of breaking. Under slow uniaxial tension at room temperature it flows at stresses near this level. Fillers and crosslink density can raise the value substantially. The number is for a common natural rubber compound.
label: Rubber
summary_short: Soft elastomeric rubber shows a low apparent yield because long polymer chains uncoil and slide instead of breaking.

description_medium: Water ice can support only a few megapascals before it begins to flow or fracture permanently under load, which is why glaciers creep on long timescales and skate blades bite into a thin stressed surface. Temperature matters enormously here; colder ice is stronger. The value is for polycrystalline ice near common terrestrial conditions rather than the deep interiors of icy moons.
label: Ice
summary_short: Water ice can support only a few megapascals before it begins to flow or fracture permanently under load, which is why glaciers creep on long timescales and skate blades bite into a thin stressed surface.

description_medium: Fired clay bricks tolerate high compression but very little ductile deformation; treating their compressive strength as a yield proxy places them around this stress scale. Masonry works because loads are kept mostly compressive and well distributed. Mortar joints and flaws dominate real walls more than the brick material alone. The value is a representative engineering-grade brick scale.
label: Brick
summary_short: Fired clay bricks tolerate high compression but very little ductile deformation; treating their compressive strength as a yield proxy places them around this stress scale.

description_medium: Lead yields at very low stress for a metal, which is why it deforms so readily under pressure and has long been useful in seals and radiation shielding where shape conformity matters. The softness comes from metallic bonding in a crystal that slips easily. Room-temperature creep is already relevant. The value is a common handbook number for pure lead.
label: Lead
summary_short: Lead yields at very low stress for a metal, which is why it deforms so readily under pressure and has long been useful in seals and radiation shielding where shape conformity matters.

description_medium: Common polyethylene yields at only a few tens of megapascals, which is why it makes flexible bottles and films instead of structural beams. Molecular weight, branching, and crystallinity all shift the exact threshold. Designers exploit the easy yielding to absorb impacts without brittle fracture. The value is representative for high-density polyethylene.
label: Polyethylene
summary_short: Common polyethylene yields at only a few tens of megapascals, which is why it makes flexible bottles and films instead of structural beams.

description_medium: Ordinary concrete carries little tensile yield because cracks propagate early, so reinforcement carries tension. In compression its apparent yield is higher due to microcrack closure and friction. Curing conditions dominate strength variation on site. The number is a compressive yield proxy for structural mixes.
label: Concrete
summary_short: Ordinary concrete carries little tensile yield because cracks propagate early, so reinforcement carries tension.

description_medium: Softwood loaded along the grain yields around this stress as lignin and cellulose microfibrils begin to slip. Across the grain the value is far lower due to anisotropy. Moisture content and knots matter greatly for real beams. The number assumes clear spruce in tension parallel to grain.
label: Wood (Soft)
summary_short: Softwood loaded along the grain yields around this stress as lignin and cellulose microfibrils begin to slip.

description_medium: ABS plastic sits in the middle ground between tough engineering polymers and disposable consumer plastics. It can take a fair amount of stress before it yields permanently, which is why it appears in housings, toys, and protective shells. Print orientation changes the number for 3D-printed parts, but molded material is more consistent. The value here is for bulk ABS at room temperature.
label: ABS Plastic
summary_short: ABS plastic sits in the middle ground between tough engineering polymers and disposable consumer plastics.

description_medium: Tendons behave viscoelastically and yield when collagen fibrils begin to slide irreversibly. Warm up raises extensibility and delays yield onset. Rehabilitation protocols keep loads well below this value for safety. The number is for bovine Achilles tendon in tension.
label: Tendon
summary_short: Tendons behave viscoelastically and yield when collagen fibrils begin to slide irreversibly.

description_medium: PLA is relatively stiff for a commodity plastic and yields at a somewhat higher stress than ABS in many room-temperature tests. That is part of why desktop 3D prints in PLA can feel crisp and rigid even when they remain somewhat brittle. Heat softens it quickly, however. The value is a representative yield stress for solid PLA.
label: PLA Plastic
summary_short: PLA is relatively stiff for a commodity plastic and yields at a somewhat higher stress than ABS in many room-temperature tests.

description_medium: Annealed copper yields at lower stress than steels but offers excellent electrical and thermal conduction. Cold work raises yield at the cost of ductility, a trade used in springs and connectors. Purity and grain size are decisive. The number is for oxygen free copper in tension.
label: Copper
summary_short: Annealed copper yields at lower stress than steels but offers excellent electrical and thermal conduction.

description_medium: Bamboo carries impressive stress along the grain because its fibers are aligned for structural efficiency. Nature effectively built a lightweight composite column long before humans named the concept. Moisture, node spacing, and species change the exact figure. The value is for mature structural bamboo loaded along the fibers.
label: Bamboo
summary_short: Bamboo carries impressive stress along the grain because its fibers are aligned for structural efficiency.

description_medium: Nylon yields when polymer chains slide past each other after straightening, a process sensitive to moisture. Conditioned samples can appear tougher but softer. Designers account for this by specifying conditioning state. The value is for dry as molded nylon 6.
label: Nylon
summary_short: Nylon yields when polymer chains slide past each other after straightening, a process sensitive to moisture.

description_medium: Cortical bone in tension yields near this stress when microcracks coalesce, while compression values are higher. Age, mineralization, and loading direction all shift the number. Implants are designed to share load to stay below this limit. The value quoted is longitudinal tension at body temperature.
label: Bone
summary_short: Cortical bone in tension yields near this stress when microcracks coalesce, while compression values are higher.

description_medium: Cast iron is strong in compression but comparatively unforgiving in tension, with little plastic range before fracture. Even so, engineering tables often place its yield-like limit in the low hundreds of megapascals for rough comparison. Historic bridges and machine frames relied on its stiffness and castability. The value here is a representative gray-iron scale.
label: Cast Iron
summary_short: Cast iron is strong in compression but comparatively unforgiving in tension, with little plastic range before fracture.

description_medium: Magnesium alloys are lighter than aluminum and can still reach respectable yield stresses for automotive and aerospace weight savings. Corrosion and flammability concerns mean design margins stay conservative. Their appeal is specific strength rather than absolute strength. The value is for a common structural magnesium alloy.
label: Magnesium Alloy
summary_short: Magnesium alloys are lighter than aluminum and can still reach respectable yield stresses for automotive and aerospace weight savings.

description_medium: Brass yields around a couple hundred megapascals depending on composition and temper, making it easy to machine and form into valves, fittings, and musical hardware. The same workability that manufacturers love also explains why brass is not used where high-strength steels dominate. Alloying with zinc tunes the tradeoff. The number is a representative cartridge-brass scale.
label: Brass
summary_short: Brass yields around a couple hundred megapascals depending on composition and temper, making it easy to machine and form into valves, fittings, and musical hardware.

description_medium: Austenitic stainless steels like 304 trade very high yield for corrosion resistance and ductility, landing near this range in the annealed condition. Cold work can push them much higher. Kitchens, chemical plants, and architecture all live in this regime. The value here is a common room-temperature figure for 304 stainless.
label: Stainless Steel (304)
summary_short: Austenitic stainless steels like 304 trade very high yield for corrosion resistance and ductility, landing near this range in the annealed condition.

description_medium: Mild low carbon steel yields at a few hundred megapascals and then work hardens, giving it a forgiving ductile plateau. This makes it ideal for beams and automobile bodies. Strain aging and temperature can introduce a Lüders band, the familiar yield point elongation. The value reflects a classic structural grade.
label: Steel (Mild)
summary_short: Mild low carbon steel yields at a few hundred megapascals and then work hardens, giving it a forgiving ductile plateau.

description_medium: Commercially pure aluminum has a modest yield, but work hardening and alloying create big gains. The value here is for a common 6061 T6 alloy in tension at room temperature using the 0.2 percent offset. Welding locally erases this strengthening unless re treated. The number is a staple in mechanical design tables.
label: Aluminum
summary_short: Commercially pure aluminum has a modest yield, but work hardening and alloying create big gains.

description_medium: Glass lacks a conventional yield in tension because flaws trigger brittle fracture before plastic flow. Under high hydrostatic pressure or in compression it can withstand much higher stresses. Surface treatments like tempering raise the effective limit. The value shown is an upper bound in compression before crushing.
label: Glass
summary_short: Glass lacks a conventional yield in tension because flaws trigger brittle fracture before plastic flow.

description_medium: Titanium alloys combine moderate density with high yield and corrosion resistance, perfect for airframes and implants. Microstructure from alpha beta processing controls the plateau. At cryogenic temperatures yield rises further. The value is for Ti 6Al 4V in the annealed condition.
label: Titanium
summary_short: Titanium alloys combine moderate density with high yield and corrosion resistance, perfect for airframes and implants.

description_medium: High-performance nickel superalloys such as Inconel 718 keep their strength at temperatures where ordinary steels soften badly. That is why turbine disks, rocket hardware, and hot-section fasteners lean on them. The metallurgy is more complicated than the round number suggests, but the design consequence is simple: they yield late. The value is a representative room-temperature yield strength.
label: Inconel 718
summary_short: High-performance nickel superalloys such as Inconel 718 keep their strength at temperatures where ordinary steels soften badly.

description_medium: High strength low alloy steels and martensitic grades push yield into the gigapascal range. Toughness becomes the balancing act to avoid brittle failures. Heat treatment recipes tune both yield and impact resistance. The number represents a quenched and tempered structural steel.
label: Steel (High Strength)
summary_short: High strength low alloy steels and martensitic grades push yield into the gigapascal range.

description_medium: Spider dragline silk is one of nature’s most impressive fibers, combining high strength with extensibility in a protein-based material. Its yield-like onset depends on humidity and exact species, but it clearly belongs in the advanced-materials range rather than the textile one. Researchers chase synthetic analogues for the same reason. The value is a representative tensile yield scale.
label: Spider Silk
summary_short: Spider dragline silk is one of nature’s most impressive fibers, combining high strength with extensibility in a protein-based material.

description_medium: Engineering ceramics exhibit very high apparent yield in compression with limited ductility. Their grain boundaries and defects set failure in tension. Designers exploit them where hot hardness matters more than give. The value is for alumina under compressive loading.
label: Ceramic
summary_short: Engineering ceramics exhibit very high apparent yield in compression with limited ductility.

description_medium: Ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene fibers sold as Dyneema or Spectra achieve multi-gigapascal strength by aligning long polymer chains. On a stress scale they compete with metals while remaining light enough to float. Ballistic protection and high-performance ropes make direct use of this. The value represents a high-grade fiber rather than the bulk plastic.
label: Dyneema Fiber
summary_short: Ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene fibers sold as Dyneema or Spectra achieve multi-gigapascal strength by aligning long polymer chains.

description_medium: Silicon carbide is a very hard ceramic that can sustain enormous compressive stress with little permanent deformation before fracture. In engineering practice that puts its effective yield-like limit in the gigapascal range. The same bonding that gives it abrasive hardness also makes it useful in armor and high-temperature applications. The value is a representative compressive strength scale.
label: Silicon Carbide
summary_short: Silicon carbide is a very hard ceramic that can sustain enormous compressive stress with little permanent deformation before fracture.

description_medium: Kevlar fiber under tension shows a high apparent yield due to oriented aromatic chains. In composites it carries loads efficiently along the fiber direction while the matrix supports shear. Impact helmets exploit this anisotropy. The number is for single fiber tensile yield.
label: Kevlar Fiber
summary_short: Kevlar fiber under tension shows a high apparent yield due to oriented aromatic chains.

description_medium: Carbon fiber composites have no single yield value; it depends on fiber direction and matrix. Along the fibers, stress at first matrix cracking is far below fiber failure. Layup design sets the usable envelope. The number is a unidirectional tensile yield along the fiber direction.
label: Carbon Fiber
summary_short: Carbon fiber composites have no single yield value; it depends on fiber direction and matrix.

description_medium: Diamond has extraordinary theoretical strength, but practical yield depends on flaws and direction. Under compression tiny samples sustain immense stresses without plasticity. Machining diamond relies on brittle fracture, not yielding. The value shown is an upper bound inferred from indentation.
label: Diamond
summary_short: Diamond has extraordinary theoretical strength, but practical yield depends on flaws and direction.

description_medium: Graphene sheets approach ideal strength at nanoscale, with yield set by breaking sp2 bonds. Defects and grain boundaries reduce the value in larger films. Experiments use nanoindenters to probe this regime. The number represents pristine monolayer strength in tension.
label: Graphene
summary_short: Graphene sheets approach ideal strength at nanoscale, with yield set by breaking sp2 bonds.

description_medium: The neutron star crust behaves like an ultra strong lattice where yield refers to the onset of plastic flow under astronomical shear. Models connect this to starquakes that glitch pulsar rotation. No terrestrial lab can reproduce the conditions. The value is a theoretical estimate.
label: Neutron Star Crust
summary_short: The neutron star crust behaves like an ultra strong lattice where yield refers to the onset of plastic flow under astronomical shear.

description_medium: Near a black hole event horizon, conventional material concepts blur, but effective stresses in accretion flows can be cast as yields. Magnetic fields and radiation pressure set the limits rather than crystalline defects. The language is metaphorical but useful for order of magnitude. The value signals a physics extreme.
label: Black Hole Horizon
summary_short: Near a black hole event horizon, conventional material concepts blur, but effective stresses in accretion flows can be cast as yields.

description_medium: Polymer foams behave like springs in a scaffold of cells, so their effective modulus is tiny until densification. Cell size, gas content, and skin layers matter as much as chemistry. Designers tune this for pillows versus helmet liners. The value is for a flexible open cell foam in small strain compression.
label: Foam
summary_short: Polymer foams behave like springs in a scaffold of cells, so their effective modulus is tiny until densification.

description_medium: Cartilage combines a collagen network with pressurized water to form a poroelastic material with low instantaneous modulus. Under sustained load the modulus rises as fluid drains. Healthy joints depend on this time dependence for shock absorption. The value is an initial small strain tangent.
label: Cartilage
summary_short: Cartilage combines a collagen network with pressurized water to form a poroelastic material with low instantaneous modulus.

description_medium: Soft rubber stores little energy per strain because chains uncoil easily, leading to a very low modulus. As strain rises, entropic elasticity stiffens the response. Fillers like carbon black raise the modulus by reinforcing the network. The value given is for an unfilled gum rubber at room temperature.
label: Rubber
summary_short: Soft rubber stores little energy per strain because chains uncoil easily, leading to a very low modulus.

description_medium: Silica aerogel is often called solid smoke because its density is so low and its stiffness is only modestly above that of soft foams. Even so, it is a true solid with a measurable elastic slope that matters in insulation panels and particle collectors. Large strains quickly move it beyond the small-strain regime. The value is a representative low-density aerogel modulus.
label: Silica Aerogel
summary_short: Silica aerogel is often called solid smoke because its density is so low and its stiffness is only modestly above that of soft foams.

description_medium: Cork compresses easily at first because gas-filled cells collapse and recover, which is why it works so well as a bottle stopper and vibration isolator. Its modulus is far above a liquid but far below wood or plastic. Moisture and direction both matter because the cell structure is anisotropic. The value is a representative small-strain modulus.
label: Cork
summary_short: Cork compresses easily at first because gas-filled cells collapse and recover, which is why it works so well as a bottle stopper and vibration isolator.

description_medium: Polyethylene is flexible because its elastic modulus is only a few hundred megapascals, several hundred times lower than common metals. That makes it ideal for bottles, cutting boards, and films that need to bend without cracking. Crystallinity shifts the stiffness a bit but not the basic scale. The value is representative for HDPE.
label: Polyethylene
summary_short: Polyethylene is flexible because its elastic modulus is only a few hundred megapascals, several hundred times lower than common metals.

description_medium: Tendon stores elastic energy for locomotion with a modulus around a gigapascal that rises with strain. Warm tissues display higher extensibility and lower stiffness initially. Training induces remodeling that tunes this property. The figure is a small strain slope for Achilles tendon.
label: Tendon
summary_short: Tendon stores elastic energy for locomotion with a modulus around a gigapascal that rises with strain.

description_medium: Softwoods are anisotropic; along the grain the modulus is moderate, across the grain it is an order lower. Moisture acts like a plasticizer that reduces stiffness. Builders season wood to stabilize this property. The value is longitudinal for dried spruce.
label: Wood (Soft)
summary_short: Softwoods are anisotropic; along the grain the modulus is moderate, across the grain it is an order lower.

description_medium: ABS plastic is noticeably stiffer than polyethylene but still far softer than metals, which is why product housings feel solid while retaining some impact tolerance. Engineers like this middle ground for consumer goods and machine covers. The modulus depends on temperature and whether the part is molded or printed. The value is a common handbook figure.
label: ABS Plastic
summary_short: ABS plastic is noticeably stiffer than polyethylene but still far softer than metals, which is why product housings feel solid while retaining some impact tolerance.

description_medium: Nylon sits in the low-gigapascal range, stiff enough for gears, fasteners, and bushings yet compliant enough to damp shock and noise. Moisture softens it because water acts as a plasticizer in the polymer network. That is why dry and conditioned values can differ noticeably in datasheets. The value is a representative small-strain modulus for nylon 6.
label: Nylon
summary_short: Nylon sits in the low-gigapascal range, stiff enough for gears, fasteners, and bushings yet compliant enough to damp shock and noise.

description_medium: PLA prints feel rigid because their elastic modulus reaches a few gigapascals, substantially above many household plastics. That helps small printed parts keep shape, though it does not guarantee toughness. Temperature softening remains the main weakness. The number is a representative modulus for solid PLA.
label: PLA Plastic
summary_short: PLA prints feel rigid because their elastic modulus reaches a few gigapascals, substantially above many household plastics.

description_medium: Water ice is much less stiff than rock or metal but far stiffer than rubber, which is why glaciers can support cracks and transmit seismic waves even while creeping over years. Planetary scientists rely on this modulus when modeling icy moons and ice shelves. Temperature shifts it meaningfully. The value is a typical terrestrial ice modulus.
label: Ice
summary_short: Water ice is much less stiff than rock or metal but far stiffer than rubber, which is why glaciers can support cracks and transmit seismic waves even while creeping over years.

description_medium: Spider dragline silk stretches more than most engineering fibers, but its modulus still lands around tens of gigapascals, high enough to store useful elastic energy in a light thread. Biologists care because that balance of stiffness and toughness is rare in natural materials. Humidity changes the feel quickly. The value is a representative dry-fiber modulus.
label: Spider Silk
summary_short: Spider dragline silk stretches more than most engineering fibers, but its modulus still lands around tens of gigapascals, high enough to store useful elastic energy in a light thread.

description_medium: Hardwoods like oak are stiffer than many softwoods because of their denser microstructure and higher latewood fraction. Furniture makers and structural engineers both feel this directly in how little a board flexes under load. Grain direction still dominates the number, so this is an along-grain figure. The value is a representative modulus for oak.
label: Oak
summary_short: Hardwoods like oak are stiffer than many softwoods because of their denser microstructure and higher latewood fraction.

description_medium: Common fired brick behaves like a stiff brittle ceramic composite on small elastic strains. Masonry design often treats whole walls rather than brick alone, but the brick material itself lives in the low tens of gigapascals. That is enough to keep arches and facades from sagging visibly under ordinary loads. The value is a representative engineering brick modulus.
label: Brick
summary_short: Common fired brick behaves like a stiff brittle ceramic composite on small elastic strains.

description_medium: Lead is soft in yield strength but not infinitely floppy: its elastic modulus still sits in the tens of gigapascals. That is why lead pipes and sheets can hold shape until creep and plasticity take over. The contrast between low modulus metals and high modulus ceramics is one of the simplest material lessons to feel by hand. The value is a standard handbook number.
label: Lead
summary_short: Lead is soft in yield strength but not infinitely floppy: its elastic modulus still sits in the tens of gigapascals.

description_medium: Bamboo is a natural fiber composite whose stiffness along the grain can rival some structural timbers and low-end engineering materials. Its geometry makes it especially effective for lightweight columns and scaffolds. Across the grain the modulus is far lower, so direction matters. The number is an along-fiber representative value.
label: Bamboo
summary_short: Bamboo is a natural fiber composite whose stiffness along the grain can rival some structural timbers and low-end engineering materials.

description_medium: Cortical bone has a modulus in the tens of gigapascals along the osteon direction due to mineralized collagen. Age and disease reduce both stiffness and toughness. Implant designers choose alloys to match this to avoid stress shielding. The value is for human femoral cortical bone in tension.
label: Bone
summary_short: Cortical bone has a modulus in the tens of gigapascals along the osteon direction due to mineralized collagen.

description_medium: Concrete’s modulus depends on aggregate and curing; it is not a pure material constant. Codes use empirical formulas tied to compressive strength. Long term creep lowers effective stiffness in service. The value is a short term tangent for a structural mix.
label: Concrete
summary_short: Concrete’s modulus depends on aggregate and curing; it is not a pure material constant.

description_medium: Magnesium alloys are attractive in vehicles and aircraft because their stiffness is lower than aluminum’s but their density is lower too. That means components can still achieve respectable specific stiffness when geometry is optimized. Corrosion protection and fatigue remain important design constraints. The value is a representative modulus for structural magnesium alloys.
label: Magnesium Alloy
summary_short: Magnesium alloys are attractive in vehicles and aircraft because their stiffness is lower than aluminum’s but their density is lower too.

description_medium: Aluminum alloys share a modulus near seventy gigapascals regardless of strength grade because stiffness depends on bonding, not microstructure alone. This constancy simplifies deflection calculations. Temperature reduces modulus slightly. The value is for a typical wrought alloy.
label: Aluminum
summary_short: Aluminum alloys share a modulus near seventy gigapascals regardless of strength grade because stiffness depends on bonding, not microstructure alone.

description_medium: Glass is relatively stiff with a modulus similar to some metals despite brittleness. Defects control strength but not this initial slope. Temperature near the glass transition softens it dramatically. The value is for soda lime glass at room temperature.
label: Glass
summary_short: Glass is relatively stiff with a modulus similar to some metals despite brittleness.

description_medium: Kevlar fibers are less stiff than carbon fibers but still very much engineering fibers, landing around tens of gigapascals in axial modulus. Their real advantage is the combination of stiffness, toughness, and low density. Ballistic fabrics and ropes turn that combination into practical products. The value is a representative fiber-direction modulus.
label: Kevlar Fiber
summary_short: Kevlar fibers are less stiff than carbon fibers but still very much engineering fibers, landing around tens of gigapascals in axial modulus.

description_medium: Brass is mechanically between aluminum and steel in stiffness, which is why instruments, fittings, and decorative hardware feel dense and solid without becoming especially springy. Composition changes the exact number, but not by an order of magnitude. Machinists value the consistency this implies. The value is a representative modulus for cartridge brass.
label: Brass
summary_short: Brass is mechanically between aluminum and steel in stiffness, which is why instruments, fittings, and decorative hardware feel dense and solid without becoming especially springy.

description_medium: Titanium alloys are roughly half as stiff as steel at similar densities, giving good specific stiffness. Designers exploit this for weight sensitive parts that must flex without yielding. Temperature and phase mix set exact values. The number is for Ti 6Al 4V.
label: Titanium
summary_short: Titanium alloys are roughly half as stiff as steel at similar densities, giving good specific stiffness.

description_medium: Copper combines excellent electrical conduction with a modulus a bit above one hundred gigapascals, enough to make busbars and springs hold form while still yielding more readily than steels. Purity and cold work change strength much more than stiffness. That separation is why electrical and mechanical design tables both matter. The value is a representative modulus for bulk copper.
label: Copper
summary_short: Copper combines excellent electrical conduction with a modulus a bit above one hundred gigapascals, enough to make busbars and springs hold form while still yielding more readily than steels.

description_medium: Crystalline silicon is the structural backbone of chips and MEMS, and its modulus is high enough that tiny beams and resonators can ring at precise frequencies. The exact value depends on crystal direction because the lattice is anisotropic. Semiconductor fabrication treats this as a design parameter, not trivia. The number is a representative orientation-averaged modulus.
label: Silicon
summary_short: Crystalline silicon is the structural backbone of chips and MEMS, and its modulus is high enough that tiny beams and resonators can ring at precise frequencies.

description_medium: Unidirectional carbon fiber composites have an effective modulus near two hundred gigapascals along the fiber direction, while transverse is far lower. Rule of mixtures gives a first estimate based on fiber volume. Layup choices tailor stiffness to load paths. The number is for a high modulus fiber epoxy lamina.
label: Carbon Fiber
summary_short: Unidirectional carbon fiber composites have an effective modulus near two hundred gigapascals along the fiber direction, while transverse is far lower.

description_medium: Steels cluster near two hundred gigapascals in modulus across many alloys and tempers. Heat treatment alters yield and toughness but not this slope much. That is why beams deflect similarly before yield regardless of grade. The value is the canonical handbook number.
label: Steel
summary_short: Steels cluster near two hundred gigapascals in modulus across many alloys and tempers.

description_medium: Engineering ceramics achieve very high modulus due to strong ionic and covalent bonds. Their stiffness remains high even at heat where metals soften. Designers trade brittleness against this stiffness for cutting tools. The value is for alumina.
label: Ceramic
summary_short: Engineering ceramics achieve very high modulus due to strong ionic and covalent bonds.

description_medium: Tungsten is one of the stiffest practical metals, which is why it holds shape at heat and finds use in filaments, weights, and tooling. Its density is famous, but the high modulus is just as important in applications that need resistance to elastic bending. Brittleness is the tradeoff. The value is a representative room-temperature modulus.
label: Tungsten
summary_short: Tungsten is one of the stiffest practical metals, which is why it holds shape at heat and finds use in filaments, weights, and tooling.

description_medium: Silicon carbide combines ceramic hardness with very high elastic stiffness, making it valuable for armor, abrasives, mirrors, and high-temperature components. Components made from it resist small elastic strain strongly before brittle failure becomes the real limit. It is a good reminder that stiffness and toughness are separate traits. The value is a representative engineering modulus.
label: Silicon Carbide
summary_short: Silicon carbide combines ceramic hardness with very high elastic stiffness, making it valuable for armor, abrasives, mirrors, and high-temperature components.

description_medium: Diamond is among the stiffest known solids because of its dense sp3 network. Small strains store huge elastic energy before fracture. Microelectromechanical resonators exploit this for high frequency stability. The value is a polycrystalline average.
label: Diamond
summary_short: Diamond is among the stiffest known solids because of its dense sp3 network.

description_medium: Graphene’s in plane modulus approaches the theoretical limit for a two dimensional lattice. Out of plane bending is much softer, illustrating geometric effects. Large area films reduce modulus due to wrinkles and defects. The value is from nanoindentation on monolayers.
label: Graphene
summary_short: Graphene’s in plane modulus approaches the theoretical limit for a two dimensional lattice.

description_medium: The crust of a neutron star has a colossal effective shear modulus in models, reflecting interactions in a dense nuclear lattice. Starquakes excite oscillations that encode this stiffness indirectly. Laboratory analogies are qualitative at best. The value is an estimate from astrophysical constraints.
label: Neutron Star Crust
summary_short: The crust of a neutron star has a colossal effective shear modulus in models, reflecting interactions in a dense nuclear lattice.

description_medium: Near a black hole horizon, describing spacetime response with an effective modulus is metaphorical yet useful for order of magnitude. Accretion disk magneto turbulence sets stress strain like relations for the fluid. These ideas guide simulations of jets and spectra. The number is a heuristic extreme for comparison.
label: Black Hole Horizon
summary_short: Near a black hole horizon, describing spacetime response with an effective modulus is metaphorical yet useful for order of magnitude.
